spans.s: Syūma-gṛbh, used of a horse in the Rigveda (vi. 36, 2) seems to mean ‘grasping the bit between his teeth,’ as a horse does when anxious to break away from control.

Syūman in one passage of the Rigveda denotes, according to Roth, the strap fastening the door of a house, the Homeric.
Foot notes iii. 61, 4.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.

Syūma-raśmi is the name of a protégé of the Aśvins in the Rigveda.
Foot notes i. 112 16; viii. 52, 2. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 150, 163.
